a.text: Can you hear Victoria cry, o kings of yore?
Fires burn my mother's skin...
I fly above her head, but do not hear her cry for help.
Only lament.
But who does she lament for—

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Don't bother collecting the bodies of the Steam Knights and mercenaries. The Victorians already built this tomb for them.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: I know, Ines, but...
Paprika clenches the blood-stained piece of paper in her hand and tries to imagine what it felt like as the Steam Knight wrote these words.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: This is the Steam Knights' home, but the Sarkaz shouldn't be left here.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: If Hoederer can really bring everyone back to Kazdel with the Lifebone, can we take them with us too?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: If you've already made up your mind, then go ahead.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: But are you sure about this, Paprika? You aren't from Kazdel.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: I—I can always find a way back to Columbia if I need to—
It's safer to travel back with the group for now.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Who knows what they'd do to you if you stayed in Victoria, or tried to head back to Columbia now?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Given the circumstances—

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Ngh!

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Stop pretending you're not injured.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I won't die. I can't die. Besides, we're already taking too long.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: How is the Lifebone's recovery going?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: It'll make it to Kazdel... provided no one 'accidentally' damages it again.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Oh, was that meant for me?

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Guess YOUR recovery's going just fine.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: How are things looking outside, W?

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I'll let you off the hook about the name this time, Ines.

spans.text: I'll let you off the hook about the name

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Even better. How are things looking outside, W?

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: The Victorians made a big push right after the fire on the walls. The Nachzehrer lines collapsed right away.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: What about the Nachzehrer King?

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Still kicking, but he retreated into the city—

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: I—Is there any news about the General, Miss Wiš'adel?

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Nope. Could be dead for all I know.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Manfred wouldn't die so easily.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: But the chaos outside is a problem.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Based on intel my guys collected, Nezzsalem is still sitting cozy, even though the Military Commission screwed this battle up big time.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: And while I'd love to blow Theresis to smithereens, I gotta admit...

spans.text: to blow Theresis to smithereens, I gotta admit...

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: He's a cunning enough bastard that there's no way his forces would back down that easy.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I'm thinking your plan needs to be moved up, Hoederer.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: The Lifebone is ready.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Whatever the Regent is scheming, we should prepare to leave with the ones who've been dragged into this mess... before the Sarkaz purge begins.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I doubt the Victorians would let them go so easily.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I know, but...

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Since when did we need the Victorians' permission to do anything?

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I've got an idea.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: But first, we'll need to capture the Commission's command center. Say, in the name of Babel.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: You guys just wait here for my orders—

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: An idea isn't a plan, W, but you seem confident.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Fine, let's go. I've spent enough time underground.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Er, doesn't Hoederer need someone to take care of him?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I have it on good authority that he won't die.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...Yes, that's what I said.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Whatever the Regent and Nachzehrer are planning at the Palace of Westhaleg, the fate of the survivors is probably not their priority.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: We can't just sit back and watch. You can tell us about your idea on the way.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Hmph. Two dunces.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: What about you, Yarnball?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: I'll go with you! The General might be at the command center. I have so much to ask him!

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: But do we just leave the Lifebone here?

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I could blow it to pieces if you want. If you're volunteering to carry everyone on your back instead.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: It's WIŠ'ADEL!

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Don't worry, Yarnball, no one'll ever guess it's here. And if anyone dares get close, my guys will take care of them.
Wiš'adel surveys the resting place of kings, now barely-recognizable rubble.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Besides, what better place to hide a pile of bones than a graveyard?

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Found a way in yet?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: The ducal alliance's army is surrounding the place, but they don't seem to have any intention of attacking.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: What are they doing, then? Out for a picnic?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Defending this place was so important to the General. How could...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: The General? You mean that devil by the name of Manfred? I'm afraid he fled with his tail between his legs, abandoning all of you.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Her Grace was right. The Military Commission's spies do come through here.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Who the hell are you calling Commission spies?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: We are not your enemies. We've come to end this war.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I've read your file, Sarkaz. 'The Right-Hand of Manfred'. Your word can hardly be taken at face value.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Then maybe you've also read how I escaped from Manfred.

spans.text: Then maybe you've also read how I

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I'm afraid I lacked the patience to read through the files of every insignificant devil.

steps.name: Alliance Soldier
steps.text: We've surrounded the place, sir.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Eliminate these Sarkaz spies.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Search their bodies for intel on the command center. I've had enough of the Sarkaz's tricks.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Hah! So you're not attacking 'cause you're too scared of what's inside?!

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Well, if you don't have the guts, we'll do it for you.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Are you sure you want to pick a fight now, W? I can ensure a safe retreat, at least.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: (Pulls weapon) I'm with her. The Sarkaz cannot afford to wait.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Protect Paprika, Ines. We're forcing our way through.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: If you say so.
Shadows spread from Ines's feet, locking on to every Victorian soldier present.
Then, she senses a different kind of shadow.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: ...Delphine?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Let them through, sir.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: And here I was thinking you finally made up your mind to kill us.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I am not under the command of the Exemplars, my lady. Nor do I want to be put on 'mandatory leave' like Bellingham. I am simply executing the Duke's orders—

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: 'Wipe out the Sarkaz.' No more, no less.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: These Sarkaz share our strategic objective.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: They aren't a monolith.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You're here to kill the Nachzehrer, aren't you, Hoederer?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: The Nachzehrer King holds great significance to the Sarkaz, but he cannot be allowed to live.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Only the swift and complete defeat of his forces will convince the ones sitting on the fence to willingly withdraw with us.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: ...You want to flee with the devils?

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Got a problem with that, punk?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You do understand the crimes they committed, do you not?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...I can't deny them.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: But I also understand what will happen if large numbers of leaderless Sarkaz mercenaries are left scattered across the countryside.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Mercenaries who've tasted blood in war.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You want to protect them.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: And prevent further chaos.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Can you give your guarantee?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: No. But she can. Babel can.
Hoederer points towards Wiš'adel.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: This war has long since lost its last justification for taking lives. It's time to bring it to an end. This has nothing to do with who I was, or who I am now.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Very well. You can go in.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: If Rhodes Island trusts you, then—

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: You should be careful, Lady Delphine. What you are doing may constitute treason.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I don't need your advice.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Lieutenant Shearer, instruct the Exemplars units to escort this Sarkaz team into the command center.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Inform all alliance units that this order comes directly from Delphine Windermere.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Understood, Lady Windermere.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I hope you will be able to answer for yourself when the Dukes hear about this.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I have even more reason to hate the Sarkaz than most of you, but I don't let it blind myself to the current situation.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Londinium has bled enough.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Thank you for your help.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: It's not you I'm helping, Sarkaz. Go end this war.

spans.text: I'm helping, Sarkaz. Go end this war.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: As for you, sir, you can either continue this staring match with me, or we can both go back with our men and prepare for the next battle.

spans.text: , you can either continue this staring match with me, or we can both go back with our men and prepare for the next battle.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Or do you need to call the Duke of Caster for instructions?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: No need for that, Lady Delphine. Her Grace has granted me discretion. I agree that this is not our battlefield.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I will, however, report all the facts pertinent to this incident to Her Grace.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Suit yourself.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: While you're at it, send her my regards, and a promise from the Exemplars—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: 'When the horn of the final battle sounds, the Exemplars will be the first to answer.'

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I get that things are messed up at the Commission, but is this really all they have guarding the command center?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: According to Dame Kal'tsit and the Doctor, Rose Riverside has probably paved the way for us.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: What about Manfred and his men? Afraid of getting blown up or something?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: If the General is still... alive, there's only one place he would be—by the Regent's side.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: We'll have to count on the Doctor's group being able to handle the Regent.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: It's all yours, Wiš'adel.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: And I thought I'd have to fight you for the mic.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Your first broadcast more than did the job. 'Wiš'adel'...

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Why so serious all of a sudden? About to spew a bunch of crap I don't understand again?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: (Shakes head) The name Her Highness gave you holds many meanings.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: If they need to hear a new voice, they'll hear it. Before that, though, I want to set things up.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: We still need the command center to organize the withdrawal. Don't blow it up in a fit of anger.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Blow it up? Of course I wanna blow it up. But there's only one of it, which means I can't try all the different ways I had planned for it.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Don't rush me, Ines. This time, I'm gonna blow it into the sky, so everyone can see it.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: See who we are, and what we want to do.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Listen up, people! Babel's captured the Military Commission's command center.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Those bastards don't know their heads from their asses right now, and nobody's got it in them to help out the crusty old Nachzehrer King.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: So quit wasting time and get those feet moving!

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Believe me or not, whatever, just step on the gas and get this over with!

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Oh, and just saying, don't forget to keep your eyes on the sky.

steps.name: Sudaram
steps.text: My Patriarch, that...

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: The command structure of the Commission has collapsed. Temporary chaos is inevitable... but no matter.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: The long oppression may have numbed the Sarkaz, but this war has reignited their hatred.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: A moment of fear or hesitation will not extinguish it.
The Nachzehrer King looks up to see a frenzied flame cut open the veil of decay for an instant.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Besides, there will be another to stand up and lead them.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: 'Babel'...

a.text: The first time I saw the Palace of Westhaleg was fifteen years ago, on a fifty-pound bill.
It was the first time I held a wrench in my hands, and the first time I held money I'd earned myself.
I rubbed the bill with my numb and tired hands. The factory door began to close behind me, but I felt as though the door to all of Terra was being opened before my eyes.
A place that seemed so far away, a place where kings once sat, was right there in my hands.

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: Why'd we stop?

steps.name: Exemplar
steps.text: The area ahead is completely shrouded in fog. Captain Horn's orders are to halt the advance until we figure what tricks the Nachzehrer are up to in there.

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: Look at all the pretty patterns on the tiles beneath our feet, though. We're close to the palace.

steps.name: Exemplar
steps.text: Be patient, and grab a proper weapon from camp. The Sarkaz protecting this place are the worst of the worst. A wrench isn't gonna cut it.

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: This wrench has smashed five Sarkaz skulls just on the way here!

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: I can do it, whether you believe it or not.

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: It's been fifteen years since I felt like this, but now... I feel like I can take that palace, Nachzehrer King be damned.

steps.name: Exemplar
steps.text: Wait... shush.

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Exemplar
steps.text: Fog. I'll report it in. Find a safe place to hide.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: You hear that sound from inside the fog?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: All I hear is the wind. Same sound as when I forgot to shut the gym's windows at night.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: If it's the wind, it's blowing against something! A flag, or clothes!

spans.text: If it's the wind, it's blowing against

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Tell Vina—
In an instant, innumerable tattered rags rush out of the fog, drifting across the sky above the city like a gray-white tide.
There is cloth freshly torn from clothing, and there are banners woven by hatred over the millennia.
They have wrapped generation after generation of Nachzehrer warriors, hiding the rot beneath, but now they fly freely in the sky, inviting all they touch to walk into decay.

steps.name: Exemplar
steps.text: Bloody hell, I can't free my leg!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I got you!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Get away from the cloth! I'll cover you!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: They'll corrode any weapons they touch! Melee units, pull back and let the casters deal with them!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: 1st and 3rd Caster Battalions! Volley on my mark!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I can't get rid of them!

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The palls are immersed in decay, the shroud drawing in death. Even the formless witchcraft of the Nachzehrer has rules that can be followed.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: But I am unable to decipher this fog...

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: It is neither Arts, nor natural.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Is this some new tactic, Logos?

options: They wouldn't wait this long to try a proven tactic.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Perhaps Nezzsalem is changing... or perhaps it's the Nachzehrer themselves that are changing.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This place will soon be more dangerous than the shroud we stepped into on the battlefield outside the city.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The other units must have encountered the same interference. Even sending out a signal is difficult.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This three-hundred meter plaza is enough to delay a thousand men for days.

options: We must find Theresis.
Theresis still has Amnannam.
Analyze the shroud, Logos.
How's our comms equipment, Closure?

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Already on it.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Rules are bound to be analyzed. There must be a source for this unusual shroud.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: I'll just need a bit of time.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: If we don't want the Nachzehrer cutting the battlefield to itty-bitty pieces in the fog, turning our offensive into more of a buffet...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: We should fill the plaza with repeaters, including those curvy corridors on the sides...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: We don't have time to get a bunch more equipment, but luckily, I have a backup plan!

a.text: I never told them that I had never killed anyone. I did exterminate a few districts' worth of musbeasts, but never a human.
I never told them that it was not an Arts-imbued pall I wrapped myself in, but rags taken from stolen mops.
After all, I had never met another Nachzehrer in all the years I grew up in the ditches of Londinium, and no one ever taught me the Nachzehrer Arts.
I wrapped myself in mops so the Victorians wouldn't beat me to death. A 'Mop-Head' that killed musbeasts for them deserved to live more than the Sarkaz, at least.

steps.name: 'Mop-Head'
steps.text: Er, why are you ripping the cloth off of yourselves?

steps.name: Nachzehrer Warrior
steps.text: Our Patriarch says we need no longer hide the decay.

steps.name: 'Mop-Head'
steps.text: Sh—Should I rip mine off too, then?

steps.name: Nachzehrer Warrior
steps.text: Of course, child.

steps.name: 'Mop-Head'
steps.text: Er... why doesn't it fly away like yours did?

steps.name: 'Mop-Head'
steps.text: Am I missing some Arts?

steps.name: Nachzehrer Warrior
steps.text: Feel the decay within you returning to the land. Feel the withered life returning to your body.

steps.name: Nachzehrer Warrior
steps.text: Then, rejoice.

steps.name: 'Mop-Head'
steps.text: So, I should rejoice...?

a.text: I beat a Nachzehrer to a pulp.
They said the Nachzehrer could never be truly killed. So I kept swinging my wrench like my life depended on it, even though the one beneath me was no longer moving.
His ugly frame was much frailer than I imagined. I broke it like the fallen branches in the snow under my feet in the winters of my childhood.
They always broke with such a satisfying crack. Was the war answering my courage?
I liked the feeling.

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: I could. I said I could.

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: Who said you can't truly kill a Nachzehrer? This one seems pretty dead to me!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Careful there! You dinnae want to be near a Nachzehrer corpse long!
The Nachzehrer warrior's body quickly collapses, losing all form and color.
An invisible fog takes up the form of the dead, and gently embraces the remains.

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: It just rots on its own? That quick?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: If we dinnae get away now, we and that body both'll be Nachzehrer food.

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: Bloody hell, and there I was, thinking the Nachzehrer weren't such bloody monsters after all...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: It'll be fine, alright! Where d'you come from? Think about home! All that sun and hay and beer, you know!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I think you'll feel a wee bit better puttin' all this rot out of your mind!

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: I'm from Londinium! All I had at home was sourdough hard enough to smash skulls!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Aye, that works!

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: Yeah, works for me!

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Death and decay are defined by silence. I never thought the Sudaram could operate so noisily.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: No longer do the Nachzehrer try to keep their nature in check. They are allowing decay to run unchecked.

options: Meaning it'll be harder to stop the spread of rot?

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: A pair of hands cannot stop rushing water.

options: But they can easily spray the water further.
What if we 'diluted' the rot, Logos?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Hang in there. You'll get better.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: AAAARRRRRGGGGHHHHH!!! DO I LOOK LIKE I'LL GET BETTER TO YOU?!

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: A natural effect of rapidly applying healing Arts.

steps.name: Forlorn Soldier
steps.text: Take this, give it to—argh! Uh—

steps.name: Forlorn Soldier
steps.text: —The pain... it's getting better?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Do not choose the end out of pain, soldier. Endure.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: The pain will stop, in time.

steps.name: Forlorn Soldier
steps.text: Thank you, Sarkaz...

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Listen to Liz, it'll be alright. In cases of acute Infection, we have to avoid rapid emotional fluctuations. Take a deep breath, and—

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Message from the Doctor, Nearl.

options: Shining, Nearl, Nightingale, are you in the rear?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: We're at the rear camp. Just returned with a bunch of wounded.

options: How is Nightingale?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Weak, but she refused to abandon the injured to their fates. We'll take care of her.

options: I need you to pull out of the area, along with everybody in camp.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Doctor, you...

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Let us know if you need any support.

options: The Nachzehrer shroud won't be easily dispelled with Arts.
We'll divert the fog of decay to nearby areas.
Do your best to ensure that no one's caught in it.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Roger.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: ...The more lives we save, the less decay there is to feed on.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: It's the duty of the Followers, isn't it?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Nearl. Shining. There's no time to rest.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Liz...
Liz's blue fowlbeast perches on Shining's shoulder, rubbing against her cheek.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: *Sigh* Sometimes I just don't know what to do with you.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Nearl?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Go and save some lives. As for the enemy—

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Leave them to my spear and shield.
'Bzzz—bzzzz—'
'Bzzzt—'

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Wow, I never knew fog could be so noisy!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The interference is too strong! Might be easier to yell than get a signal through!

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: We can't place the repeaters directly on the ground! The fog eats away at the antennae!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: If we put up a shield...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: No, with interference like this, that'd just block whatever's left of the signal.

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: What if we carried the repeaters?

steps.name: Fang
steps.text: The fog won't eat at the equipment as long as we're still alive, right?
Closure clenches her comms terminal tightly, but she can feel the pain of its metal corners biting into her skin fading away. Her limbs are becoming numb.
The fog clings to all life equally, inviting them to join the procession of decay.
She knows what Fang's suggestion implies. She wants to reject it.
But she does not.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: You go. I'll stay here with the base station.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Think, Closure, think! If this fog is from Nachzehrer Arts, then that can't just be meaningless noise.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Identify the pattern, and we can filter it out!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: There it is! It's not noise, it's the voice of the Nachzehrer!
Even if their flesh has decayed, even if their consciousness has long faded, the lifeforce of the Nachzehrer continues to sing in joy as they return to the Cycle.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: No idea what you're so happy about, but I'm sick of hearing it!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Lemme see... a little more over here...
'Bzzz—bzzzz—'
'Clo—sure—bzzz'

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I'm getting a signal! But it's still not enough...

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: How about this?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: That's what I'm talking about! Wait, Misery? How did you...?

steps.name: Misery
steps.text: I can cut a path through the fog for communications.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Great! Now we can hear what—

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: 3rd Caster Battalion! Engage the Nachzehrer emerging from behind the lines!

steps.name: 'The Young Duke'
steps.text: Don't let them cut us off from the Exemplars!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The weight-bearing structures of the corridors to the sides of the plaza are heavily damaged! They're about to collapse!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Watch out for falling debris!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The whole battlefield...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: ...It's connected.

a.text: Now I have killed. A Victorian girl wearing a bright printed scarf on her head.
Her scarf faded and her complexion twisted before my face. She became no different from the musbeasts I killed, only bigger and more hollow.
Her life must have flowed into me. I find myself swinging the greatsword that they gave me, almost as tall as I am.
But I don't feel the ecstasy they spoke of.

steps.name: 'Mop-Head'
steps.text: AHHH—!

steps.name: 'Mop-Head'
steps.text: Phew—you, you're rotten too.

steps.name: 'Mop-Head'
steps.text: If I don't rot, you will, is that it?

steps.name: 'Mop-Head'
steps.text: Wh—What's that?
The massive explosion almost ruptures the young Nachzehrer's eardrums. A massive suit of armor flies past him.
The fog gently picks away the broken limbs the armor is wearing, pale fragments dispersing with the steam.
Several Sudarams fly towards it, their swords making screeching sounds on the metal, piercing the dull thud of Originium explosives.

steps.name: Steam Knight
steps.text: (Sound of gushing steam)

steps.name: Sudaram
steps.text: Metal... shall... decay...
The young Nachzehrer has no time to look back. Heavy metal legs break the fog in front of him, blocking out the already-dim sunlight.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: How many years do you think it took us to build The Crawler? You think we'd just let you eat it?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Armor plate to the portside foreleg!

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Does the main gun still turn? Two o'clock, fire!

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Blast a path through the Sudaram for the Steam Knight!
The young Nachzehrer falls to the ground. Cold blood immediately seeps through the remaining mop cloth, as though he was born to wipe such filth.
But why was he born to?
He has no time to think about the answer. A great iron hammer is raised above his head, its glaring reflection in his eyes.

steps.name: 'Mop-Head'
steps.text: No, no—

steps.name: 'Mop-Head'
steps.text: I don't want to—
You don't want to die.
A tide of rot rushes past him, and the hammer falls to the ground as scrap.

steps.name: 'Mop-Head'
steps.text: M—My Patriarch...?

steps.name: 'Mop-Head'
steps.text: I—I'm sorry, I'm not, I didn't...

steps.name: 'Mop-Head'
steps.text: Please, don't punish me... I'm not a deserter, I just—

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: If you have yet to fully comprehend war, then you are no deserter. It is not yours to give up your life so easily in.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Your war has yet to come.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Go.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The fog... it's fading.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: More and more wounded are being evacuated before they die. The Nachzehrer are being deprived of the rot they feed on.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: 'Disperse.'

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The fog is thinning.

options: Even I can breathe now.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Wait, you couldn't breathe all this time, Doctor?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Why didn't you say anything?

options: It wasn't that bad. It's just better now.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This won't last for long. Shining reports that the fog that had been diverted elsewhere is returning.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We must move—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor—!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr!

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: 'Perish.'

a.text: You feel a sense of deja vu.
It is not that any memories came back to you. It is that, once again, you sense how tiny and frail your life is.
A blade of grass in the wilderness. What is one blade or a thousand in the presence of death? You will all become nutrition for next year's sprouts.
The tide of rot crosses Amiya's black curtain, Mon3tr's massive frame, and Logos's wall of incantations, rushing towards you.
The next instant, it comes to an abrupt halt.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: It is you.

options: It is me.
What?

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: You have kept your promise.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr, Structural Fortification! Protect the Doctor!

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: There is no need, Dame. I shall not fight you here.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Even though this is a battlefield?

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Precisely because it is a battlefield.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: You do not belong to this battlefield of mine. Every second you spend here is an insult to it.

options: War doesn't belong to anyone. It only destroys everyone.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Hah! How arrogant.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: No matter. This war that has nurtured me, this war I have nurtured, is now over.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Even if it has cycled back and forth for a thousand years in the most uninteresting manner, even if the pain it gave rise to has become numbness, this war has achieved its goal.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Now, the Sarkaz are masters of their own destiny.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Amnannam in Theresis's hands...

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Theresis? No. The Amnannam is in the hands of all Sarkaz, scattered across the land for a thousand years.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: From this war, they will come away with power, freedom, and a future.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: What is left for me is the purest afterglow of war, one that knows no purpose but war itself.

spans.text: is the purest afterglow of war, one that knows no purpose but war itself.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If there is no purpose, then why do you—

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Outblood child, so eager to put a stop to everything you do not wish to see.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: If you see war as only evil, suffering as only a mistake, and sacrifice as only a waste, then you can bring neither destruction nor rebirth.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...Should I take this as the God of War advising the King of Sarkaz?

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Very good! Finally, you call yourself king.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: But it is not advice. My war may have won the Sarkaz a future, but it is not my place to dictate what it is.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: My place is only to fulfill the very nature of my being.

options: To spread decay?
To nurture new life?

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: To me, decay and rebirth are one and the same.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: As for you, ageless dame, outblood king, and you... It is not my place to judge you.

spans.text: As for you, ageless dame, outblood king, and
... It is not my place to judge you.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Go. Theresis awaits.
Behind the Nachzehrer King, the ranks of Sarkaz part silently.
They reveal a black path between white shroud, white bones, and white pall.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Doctor.

options: Only by taking down Theresis and Amnannam...
...will we truly bring an end to this calamity.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We're with you, Doctor.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This is the moment Rhodes Island has prepared for. There is no need to hesitate.

options: And... the Nachzehrer King?

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: My whistle shall disperse the fog.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: If we triumph, we will not celebrate victory alone.

a.text: Through the fog, you can see the faint silhouette of a tank, the gushing steam of a Steam Knight, Exemplars and alliance soldiers fighting side-by-side—
You hear the communications of Closure, Wiš'adel, and the others—
All of them fighting for the same end...

options: —An end to this war.
Let's go meet Theresis.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: You have crossed the waters of death, Aefanyl, and witnessed the dim candlelight of the other side.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Go. I do not wish to fight you.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Sing once more when all decay has returned to the soil, when all war drums are silent.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Your end does not lie here.
The Banshee shakes his head and says nothing. His bone pen floats up in front of him.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Hah. So be it.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: ...I do envy Laqeramaline.
The Nachzehrer King spreads his arms wide. The Banshee begins to move his bone pen.
A thousand branches rise from the Nachzehrer, formed of flesh, blood, and bone. A thousand incantations are etched by the point of the Banshee's pen, in opposition to the decay.

A thousand branches spread out on the battlefield. Every Nachzehrer corpse they touch, from the ethereal remains of the ancient Sudaram, to the yet-unrotted flesh of young Nachzehrer warriors, blooms in flowers of decay.
Once again, the Nachzehrer rise from decay.
Once again, the fearless charge forth in the incantations of the Banshee.

a.text: The Palace of Westhaleg... It wasn't grand at all.
In fact, it looks even more decrepit than what I saw on that bill fifteen years ago.
The blood and flesh covering my hands feels more real. I stopped counting the number of Sarkaz I put down. It must've been a lot, because my wrench broke.

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: I see him! That must be the Nachzehrer King!

steps.name: Exemplar
steps.text: Wait... This is as far as I can go.

steps.name: Exemplar
steps.text: *Cough* You can't charge in bare-handed. Take this sword.

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: Th—The Sighs of Kings—

a.text: My daughter liked to rub my arm when I was lying face-down on the bed. She said it was fun because my muscles were so hard.
I would pat her shoulder and tell her she could become just as strong, strong enough to lift a whole pile of steel bars.
Holding the sword in my hand, I stab at the mountain of branches under me, and climb it.

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: But how do I reach an enemy floating in mid-air?

steps.name: Steam Knight
steps.text: (Quick puff of steam)

steps.name: Steam Knight
steps.text: For Victoria!!!

a.text: I see the Steam Knight charge towards death.
I hear a sharp whistle in my ear.
I feel the ground tremble from the guns of the tank...
The elusive, terrifying white figure in the sky stops for an instant. Then the Steam Knight dives from the sky, sending the Nachzehrer King crashing to the ground.

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: He... He's so close...

a.text: I am beginning to fall in love with war—I leap from the mountain of branches, and put the sword through the Nachzehrer King.
I can even feel my eyes burn at the heat gushing from the Steam Knight as it breathes.

steps.name: 'Big Wrench'
steps.text: *Pant*... *pant*...

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Victorian... you have learned to draw life from war.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Now, you must learn to return it to war.

a.text: Hah. It was no use at all.
I am thrown a great distance. I can no longer feel my own body.
I see the Nachzehrer King once again rise into the sky, the Steam Knight wrapped in a frenzy of white cloth...
The strange Sarkaz casting his Arts, cutting a path towards the Nachzehrer King...
Familiar faces treading the death-filled path, towards that seemingly insurmountable foe with no hint of hesitation—
The fog seems to be dispersing. I see the massive four-legged tank advance... Why is there a golden-haired Kuranta here?
What are those strange contraptions that have appeared on the battlefield, making a strange sound?
I see Her Highness, our hero, Vina Victoria, the returned king, leading more and more people forward...
'For Victoria!'
I seem to see the end of the war.
The Nachzehrer King's silhouette overlaps with the sun. It is bright. Before him gathers those eager to end the war—
I can no longer see what happens next... where did the sword go?
Sorry, my girl... your daddy's not coming home.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: So you've chosen to answer Theresis's call to arms.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Even though the war will destroy you...

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Has your crown shown you my end, Your Highness?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No. We simply understand full well that the only end of war is destruction.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: What is there to fear in destruction?

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: The first Nachzehrer learned our purpose when he rose from the ashes of war.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: 'I am the end of all things.'

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: The great boulder of war sits above our heads on the slopes of time. All we can do is push it with all our might.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: This time, however, Theresis has promised me an end to the cycle.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: As had you. Do you remember?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I do, at the founding of the Military Commission.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But we have found another path.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Then prove it to me, Your Highness. I will wait.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Even if you do not find your end, however, I will carve out another path for the Sarkaz—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I can see your emotions. You are excited about this path.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: I have waited too long, since that war two hundred years ago.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Farewell, Your Highness. I will witness the conclusion of your dispute with the Regent.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: ...Babel will return.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: I have never doubted it. Nor have I doubted your promise.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Farewell.
The rays of dawn shine from the pinnacle of the Palace of Westhaleg.
They drive away the fog, revealing the aftermath of battle.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The fog is gone.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: So is the Nachzehrer King.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Did we win? He's dead, right?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: ...Innit?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I still sense that suffocating presence.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: ...We'll need to get used to it. There is much to be done.
The daybreak was unfamiliar to those returning home, or to those on the battlefield.
Morning rays pour down like blood, over the carpet of bodies on the ground.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Is this what the sunrise always looked like in Londinium?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: No... never.
The cold dawn pours blood toward the skyline, toward the winding mountains in the distance, like an ocean of blood.
The few cries of joy from the crowd quickly fall silent. This is not how anyone imagined the glory of victory.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: It's over.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: But who can truly kill war?

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: No one can kill war.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: Do you still sense his presence, Your Highness?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: He has unfortunately given himself to death. But you are correct. War will never end.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: He merely left because this particular war is over.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I almost envy him.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: He has taken so many people along with him, all to enjoy a war that belonged only to him.

steps.name: Duke of Wellington
steps.text: I have lost another fine opponent.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Tch. Guess the old man really is dead.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: No time to mull over it. The Victorians could begin their purge at any moment.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: There's a lot on your mind.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: There's just something I'm not sure about.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I have this feeling that, when the next war to change the history of Terra comes—

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: No, I'm probably overthinking it.
In the silence, only the lonely sound of a bone whistle reaches the pitch-black underground throne room.
It is the Banshee's elegy for the dead.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Is the Regent gone?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: ...Did you hear it? What is your true plan?
There is no answer. The Regent of Kazdel, the one who began this war, is not here.
He closes his eyes and seems to see a river of blood flowing towards the sky.
Manfred cannot even tell what became of the Sarkaz hero who left so many legends behind.
But he sees an image in his mind's eye—
When the fires of war once again ravage Kazdel, death shall emerge from the mountains on the skyline.
